bugs: Ordinary request inspection could dispose, lease or fail the queue before admission, without admission rechecking that state.
Capacity enforcement called an overridable public pendingCount getter instead of reading authoritative private state.
Promise-returning executors and observers failed the queue but their rejections were not consumed, for both ordinary and leased delivery.

observations: Disposed and newly leased queues executed the outer request instead of rejecting it.
A newly failed queue retained an extra outer request instead of rejecting admission.
A replaced pendingCount getter allowed nested work past capacity one.
Four executor/observer and ordinary/leased combinations failed to install a rejection handler.
before.testMethod: Promise tests use plain callback functions because vi.fn observes returned promises and would mask missing queue rejection handling. A test-owned rejection handler prevents pre-fix unhandled errors; a synchronous then spy verifies the queue installs its own handler.

fix: Recheck disposal, active lease and failure after canonical request inspection, before sequence assignment or payload retention.
Use private pending length and drain state for the capacity bound.
Reuse shared rejection containment at all four callback return sites, preserving terminal failure, quarantined followers and no replay.

verification.typecheck: passed (production and test sources); corrected a test-only generic inference error

limits: Async callbacks remain unsupported. Consuming their rejections does not cancel work already started by an invalid callback.
Request inspection reentrancy and replaced getter regressions use controlled unit-test inputs.
The separate intermittent WebKit numeric fault remains unresolved; native instrumentation remained paused.
No full release qualification, commit, push or publication is claimed.
